ai_summary: Scotland's clean power generation highlights a stark regional contrast across the transmission system today, with Scottish carbon intensity recording 0 gCO2/kWh versus 142 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. Strong wind conditions have lifted estimated Scottish wind output to 4.2 GW, representing 41.6% of installed Scottish wind capacity and contributing significantly to the total GB wind output of 10.4 GW. Nevertheless, cross-border transmission grid limits prevent this clean electricity from flowing freely to southern demand centres. As a consequence, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 85.6 GWh through Balancing Mechanism bids, accumulating an immediate constraint cost of about £2,399,049. Replacing this curtailed volume required an estimated 16,258,604 m3 of gas burned elsewhere, releasing 29,950 tonnes of CO2 that would otherwise have been avoided. Annualising this single-day constraint expenditure indicates an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £876 million. Factoring this expense across Great Britain's annual electricity volume, constraint management increases everybody's invoice in the UK by an estimated £3/MWh, demonstrating how transmission bottlenecks simultaneously inflate consumer energy bills and national carbon emissions.
